title: Director of Sales

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: With General Formulations actively exhibiting at ISA Expo 2025 and PRINTING United Expo, partnering with PDAA for vehicle wrap training certification, and wrapping 120+ LA Metro buses, the Director of Sales is on the front lines hearing customer demands for longer-lasting, graffiti-resistant solutions. This role would champion expanding Tedlar usage because: (1) sales teams likely face price objections on premium products—Tedlar's 12-20 year lifespan and reduced TCO provide compelling ROI stories to justify premium pricing and close deals, (2) they hear direct customer complaints about competitive laminates failing prematurely (fading, cracking, graffiti damage)—expanding Tedlar coverage gives them a proven solution to win back lost accounts, (3) the vehicle wrap and transit markets (where GF already uses Tedlar in GF 108 and MetroMark 209) are growing—sales leadership would want to expand the Tedlar-backed product portfolio to capture more fleet and transit RFPs requiring 7-10+ year warranties, (4) co-exhibiting with DuPont Tedlar at ISA 2025 signals joint go-to-market potential—sales leadership would want to leverage this partnership for co-selling, case studies, and competitive positioning. This role directly benefits from having more premium, differentiated products to sell into their established distribution channels across North America and global markets.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As Director of Sales, [Name] leads revenue generation across General Formulations' North America and global distribution channels (US, Canada, LATAM, APAC, Europe). They likely own sales targets, gross margin objectives, and customer retention metrics. This role influences product portfolio decisions based on market feedback and competitive intelligence from the field. They manage relationships with key accounts (transit authorities like LA Metro, fleet customers, sign manufacturers) and oversee the sales team attending major trade shows like ISA Expo and PRINTING United. They report to C-level leadership (likely CEO/President or Chief Commercial Officer) and directly manage regional sales managers and potentially key account executives.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given GF's current Tedlar product (GF 108 anti-graffiti laminate) and market presence, [Name] would specifically care about expanding Tedlar into: (1) Transit interior graphics beyond the existing MetroMark 209 bus wraps—wall panels, ceiling graphics, and protective coverings for rail and bus interiors where graffiti resistance and easy cleaning are critical for municipal contracts, (2) Architectural wall protection for commercial buildings, healthcare facilities, and public spaces where GF's existing wall film customers are experiencing maintenance headaches with non-Tedlar alternatives, (3) Premium vehicle wrap and fleet graphics SKUs that can command higher margins by offering 15-20 year warranties instead of 7-10 years, directly addressing fleet managers' total cost of ownership concerns, (4) Outdoor signage overlaminates for GF's sign manufacturer customers who are losing bids to competitors offering longer warranty periods. Each use case directly addresses pricing objections [Name]'s team faces by providing quantifiable ROI stories around fewer replacements and lower maintenance costs.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns revenue growth targets, gross margin percentage, customer acquisition and retention rates, and win/loss ratios on competitive bids. They personally care about: (1) Equipping their sales team with differentiated products that justify premium pricing and overcome commoditization pressure in the pressure-sensitive media market, (2) Reducing customer churn caused by product performance issues—if non-Tedlar laminates are generating complaints about fading, cracking, or graffiti damage, it directly threatens account retention and referrals, (3) Winning high-value transit and fleet RFPs that require 10+ year performance guarantees, which their team currently can only bid on with limited GF 108/MetroMark SKUs, (4) Maximizing the ROI of their ISA Expo and PRINTING United trade show investments by having a broader Tedlar-backed portfolio to showcase. Tedlar's graffiti resistance, UV stability, and proven field performance directly solve [Name]'s pain points around competitive differentiation and closing premium-priced deals.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: General Formulations just exhibited at ISA Expo 2025 in April (Booth #725) showcasing Economy Film & Laminate Solutions, and co-exhibited with DuPont Tedlar featuring jointly developed anti-graffiti products. They are confirmed exhibitors at PRINTING United Expo 2025. This creates immediate relevance: (1) Post-ISA Expo follow-up window—sales teams are actively following up on leads and prospects are evaluating products demonstrated at the show, making NOW the perfect time to discuss expanding the Tedlar portfolio based on customer feedback collected at the booth, (2) PRINTING United Expo preparation—with another major show approaching, [Name] would be finalizing which products to feature and sales training for the team, creating urgency to lock in new Tedlar SKUs for launch/promotion, (3) The recent DuPont-GF joint booth presence signals deepening strategic partnership momentum—capitalizing on this co-marketing success to expand collaboration is timely and logical next step.

personalization_hooks.hook: General Formulations co-exhibited with DuPont Tedlar at ISA Expo 2025, featuring jointly developed anti-graffiti products and interactive challenges between booths
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference the successful ISA partnership and booth engagement, then pivot to discussing how to build on that momentum by expanding the Tedlar portfolio beyond GF 108 to give [Name]'s sales team more premium SKUs to sell. Position this as the natural next step in the strategic partnership that was publicly showcased at ISA.

personalization_hooks.hook: GF's sales team partners with PDAA for vehicle wrap training certification and has wrapped 120+ LA Metro buses, indicating strong presence in transit and fleet markets where long-term warranties are critical
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Acknowledge their leadership in the transit/fleet segment and frame the conversation around how expanding Tedlar into more transit interior and architectural SKUs would help them win municipal and fleet RFPs requiring 10-15 year performance guarantees—a growing requirement in public sector procurement.

personalization_hooks.hook: Director of Sales hears firsthand customer complaints about competitive laminates failing prematurely and faces price objections when selling premium products without clear ROI justification
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with empathy about the challenge of justifying premium pricing in a commoditized market, then position expanded Tedlar adoption as the solution that arms their sales team with quantifiable TCO stories (fewer replacements, reduced maintenance) to overcome price objections and win competitive deals on value, not just cost.

recommended_approach: Lead with the ISA Expo partnership success and post-show momentum. Frame the conversation around expanding the existing Tedlar relationship to give [Name]'s sales team more premium, differentiated products to sell—specifically targeting transit interior, architectural wall protection, and premium vehicle wrap applications where GF already has customers but limited Tedlar penetration. Emphasize competitive differentiation and closing high-value deals, not technical specs.
